Tukey-Kramer Simultaneous Confidence Intervals for Pairwise Contrasts

Source: R/ci_tukey_kramer.R
ci_tukey_kramer.Rd

Computes the Tukey-Kramer simultaneous confidence intervals for all \(a (a - 1) / 2\) pairwise contrasts among \(a\) group means in a one-way design with possibly unequal group sample sizes (Tukey, 1953; Kramer, 1956; Hayter, 1984), and returns the result in tidy long form. Each interval has individual coverage at least the specified conf_level and the family-wise coverage is at least conf_level.

Usage

ci_tukey_kramer(x, group = NULL, conf_level = 0.95)

Arguments

x

Either (a) a fitted lm or aov object with a single one-way factor predictor, or (b) a numeric vector of observations, in which case group must also be supplied.

group

When x is a vector, a factor (or coercible to factor) of group labels, same length as x.

conf_level

Family-wise confidence level. Default 0.95.

Value

A data.frame with one row per pairwise contrast. Columns: contrast (e.g., "B - A"), mean_difference, se, q_statistic (the studentized-range \(q\)), ci_lower, ci_upper, p_adjusted.

Details

Formula. For groups \(i, j\) with means \(\bar y_i, \bar y_j\) and sample sizes \(n_i, n_j\), the Tukey-Kramer simultaneous CI is $$\bar y_i - \bar y_j \;\pm\; q_{\alpha, a, \nu} \sqrt{\frac{\mathit{MS}_E}{2} \left(\frac{1}{n_i} + \frac{1}{n_j}\right)},$$ where \(q_{\alpha, a, \nu}\) is the upper \(\alpha\) quantile of the studentized-range distribution with \(a\) groups and \(\nu\) error degrees of freedom. The quantile is base R's qtukey where that is accurate and the exact quantile where it is not: qtukey and ptukey lose accuracy at small error df (fewer than 9 for up to 6 groups, rising by steps to fewer than 111 with more than 3000 groups), above 10000 and up to \(10^8\) df, at confidence levels above .999, and, with more than 50 groups, below the .75 point of the distribution (.80 with more than 1000 groups; with 20 groups and 2 error df, qtukey(.99, 20, 2) is 44.526 where the exact value is 37.943), and qtukey can stop short of its root anywhere. There the distribution function is computed by integrating the probability integral of the range against the chi square distribution of the error variance, and the quantile is its root. cv_tukey_hsd describes the computation, the regions, and how they were measured.

Why Tukey-Kramer. Hayter (1984) proved that the Tukey-Kramer procedure is conservative for unbalanced designs (the coverage probability is at least conf_level). For balanced designs it reduces to Tukey's HSD and the coverage is exactly conf_level.

Adjusted p-values. Each pairwise \(p\)-value is computed from the studentized-range distribution, \(p = P(Q_{a, \nu} > |q|)\), by the same computation as the quantile (ptukey where it is accurate, the exact distribution function where it is not).

References

Hayter, A. J. (1984). A proof of the conjecture that the Tukey-Kramer multiple comparisons procedure is conservative. Annals of Statistics, 12(1), 61–75.

Kramer, C. Y. (1956). Extension of multiple range tests to group means with unequal numbers of replications. Biometrics, 12(3), 307–310.

Tukey, J. W. (1953). The problem of multiple comparisons. Unpublished manuscript, Princeton University.

Examples

# 1. Balanced one-way: the six marketing panels of the test_market
#    data, four outlets per panel, so the procedure is exactly Tukey's
#    HSD. Panels 5 and 6 separate from panel 1.
fit <- lm(brand_movement ~ panel, data = test_market)
ci_tukey_kramer(fit)
#>  contrast mean_difference se    q_statistic ci_lower ci_upper p_adjusted
#>  2 - 1    0.110           0.269 0.409       -1.097   1.317    0.9997    
#>  3 - 1    0.685           0.269 2.550       -0.522   1.892    0.4882    
#>  4 - 1    0.870           0.269 3.238       -0.337   2.077    0.2481    
#>  5 - 1    1.245           0.269 4.634       0.038    2.452    0.0411    
#>  6 - 1    1.295           0.269 4.820       0.088    2.502    0.0315    
#>  3 - 2    0.575           0.269 2.140       -0.632   1.782    0.6607    
#>  4 - 2    0.760           0.269 2.829       -0.447   1.967    0.3797    
#>  5 - 2    1.135           0.269 4.225       -0.072   2.342    0.0725    
#>  6 - 2    1.185           0.269 4.411       -0.022   2.392    0.0562    
#>  4 - 3    0.185           0.269 0.689       -1.022   1.392    0.9961    
#>  5 - 3    0.560           0.269 2.084       -0.647   1.767    0.6840    
#>  6 - 3    0.610           0.269 2.271       -0.597   1.817    0.6055    
#>  5 - 4    0.375           0.269 1.396       -0.832   1.582    0.9162    
#>  6 - 4    0.425           0.269 1.582       -0.782   1.632    0.8674    
#>  6 - 5    0.050           0.269 0.186       -1.157   1.257    1.0000    
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%, simultaneous interval (Tukey)

# 2. Same data via vector / group interface:
ci_tukey_kramer(test_market$brand_movement, group = test_market$panel)
#>  contrast mean_difference se    q_statistic ci_lower ci_upper p_adjusted
